title: Osteomyelitis: Diagnosis, Culture Pathway and Specialist Referral

evidenceAudit.scope: Osteomyelitis: Diagnosis, Culture Pathway and Specialist Referral
findings: Built as an additive Disease Management version using the approved-topic structure.
Investigations are ordered from bedside/laboratory assessment to imaging and specialist tests.
The original outline remains current; this version is non-current and pending clinical review.
unverifiedSections: The IDSA source is specific to native vertebral osteomyelitis; other anatomical pathways need site-specific guidance.
Saudi antimicrobial doses, durations and SFDA status require local verification.

pathophysiology.summary: Bone infection arises by bloodstream spread, contiguous infection or direct inoculation. Necrotic bone and abscess impair antimicrobial penetration and may require drainage/debridement. Microbiological diagnosis permits targeted therapy and reduces unnecessary broad-spectrum exposure.
keyMechanisms: Bone infection arises by bloodstream spread, contiguous infection or direct inoculation.
Necrotic bone and abscess impair antimicrobial penetration and may require drainage/debridement.
Microbiological diagnosis permits targeted therapy and reduces unnecessary broad-spectrum exposure.

symptoms: Focal bone pain, fever, impaired function or non-healing wound.
physicalSigns: Local tenderness, swelling, sinus, wound depth or neurological deficit when the spine is involved.
redFlags: Sepsis, neurological deficit, spinal instability, epidural collection, prosthetic infection or critical limb ischaemia.
precipitants: Recent bacteraemia, surgery/implant, diabetic ulcer, pressure injury, trauma, dialysis or injection drug use.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Destructive lesion without microbiological evidence; biopsy may be required.
Neuropathy with joint destruction and less systemic inflammation.

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Obtain at least two sets when haematogenous disease or sepsis is suspected.

ruleIn.testName: Full blood count, C-reactive protein and ESR
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Inflammatory response; normal results do not fully exclude chronic disease
Late cortical destruction, periosteal reaction or implant change
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Baseline and alternative diagnosis; early disease may be normal.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Marrow signal abnormality, abscess or epidural extension
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Preferred cross-sectional test for suspected vertebral/deep osteomyelitis.

ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Obtain before antibiotics when stable; urgent treatment overrides delay in sepsis or neurological compromise.

clinicalManagement.title: Assess urgency
actions: Check sepsis, neurovascular status, spinal neurology, wound/implant and source.
Call surgery urgently for neurological compromise, instability, abscess, necrosis or limb threat.

clinicalManagement.title: Secure microbiology
actions: Take blood cultures and obtain bone/deep tissue rather than superficial swabs.
Do not delay antibiotics in sepsis, shock or progressive neurological deficit.

clinicalManagement.title: Target treatment
actions: Select intravenous/oral therapy with infectious diseases and microbiology according to organism, site, implant, renal function and Saudi antibiogram.
Plan drainage, debridement or implant management when required.

medicationPlan.note: Antimicrobial choice and duration are site-, pathogen-, implant- and susceptibility-dependent. Do not copy a single empirical regimen across vertebral, diabetic-foot, haematogenous and postoperative osteomyelitis; use the Saudi hospital osteomyelitis/OPAT protocol after cultures.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Blood culture or image-guided/operative bone specimen identifies the pathogen where feasible.

teaching.scope: Osteomyelitis: Diagnosis, Culture Pathway and Specialist Referral
learningObjectives: Recognise the emergency and relevant red flags.
Select the correct investigation and escalation pathway.
Use medicines only within the stated branch and local formulary.
pitfalls: Delaying specialist escalation while waiting for a non-essential test.
Using an unverified medicine dose or applying an adult pathway to a child.
Mistaking publication status for clinical approval.
keyPoints: Sepsis, neurological deficit, spinal instability, epidural collection, prosthetic infection or critical limb ischaemia.

patientEducation: Explain prolonged therapy, adherence, line/wound care and red flags.
lifestyleAndDiet: Smoking cessation, nutrition and diabetes/pressure care optimisation.
mdtReferrals: Orthopaedics/spinal surgery by site, infectious diseases, microbiology, vascular/podiatry and OPAT.
dischargeCriteria: Stable, source-control decision complete and monitored antimicrobial/follow-up plan documented.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Clinical, inflammatory-marker and site-specific imaging follow-up; avoid routine repeat MRI when improving unless indicated.
